title: How to Unlock a PDF You Own
excerpt: Remove supported password protection with a known password and permission, then verify the saved copy without storing the password.
seoDescription: Remove supported password protection with a known password and permission, then verify the saved copy without storing the password.
author: The MY PDF FIX Team
body:
## Start with authorization and a known password

[Unlock PDF](/unlock-pdf) removes supported password protection from a new copy when you have permission to do so. It is not a password cracker or a recovery service. Ownership of a downloaded file is not automatically permission to bypass a publisher's or employer's restrictions.

An opening password can be different from an owner/permissions password. Some PDFs open for viewing without prompting but restrict changes. Such a file may still need an appropriate owner password for the requested operation. The tool reports failures instead of pretending that every encrypted PDF is supported.

## Example: prepare your own encrypted report for merging

Suppose you created a report, encrypted it in your document application and now need to append an authorized appendix. Keep the protected original first.

1. Open [Unlock PDF](/unlock-pdf) and select the report.
2. Enter the known password in **PDF password**. Do not put it in a filename, a support message or a URL.
3. Confirm the authorization checkbox after checking that you have permission.
4. Click **Process**. A wrong password, damaged file or unsupported encryption should produce an error, not a usable “unlocked” download.
5. Download the result and close the original reader window. Open the new copy separately: it should open without the old opening-password prompt when removal succeeded.
6. Check the page count, text, visible form values and any features you depend on. Then use [Merge PDF](/merge-pdf) for the report and appendix if needed.

Rewriting can invalidate digital signatures. Keep the original signed or encrypted file separately and do not treat the unlocked copy as identical evidence of a signature.

## What happens to the password here

The attempt is processed in your browser. The application does not upload the password or document contents, save the password in browser storage, or include it in the download filename. The password field is cleared after an attempt. This does not protect you from a compromised device, clipboard manager or malicious browser extension.

Loading website code can still make network requests, which is a different question from uploading document data. See the [Privacy Policy](/privacy) for website requests and optional services.

## Common mistakes

Do not repeatedly guess someone else's password. If you created the file, obtain the password from your password manager or document workflow. If the file belongs to another organization, request an authorized unlocked copy instead.

Do not share the unlocked download as though it still has opening protection. If protection is needed after editing, use a separate encryption-capable application; [the password-protection guide](/blog/protect-pdf-with-password) explains that PDF Fix Hub does not add encryption.

## Troubleshooting a rejected file

Check whether you entered the opening password or a different permissions password. Verify capitalization and accidental spaces without pasting a real password into a public support channel. Try the protected original in a trusted PDF reader to distinguish a damaged file from a password problem.

Unsupported encryption, certificate-based security and specialized document workflows may require the originating application. Do not rename another file type to “.pdf” or assume an empty opening password means the file has no restrictions.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can the tool recover a forgotten password?** No. It requires a valid password where one is needed.

**Will forms remain interactive?** Supported test cases retain form fields, but inspect your own result before relying on it. Flattening is a separate choice in other tools.

**Is it safe to send the original to support?** Do not send private documents or passwords. Report the tool name, browser and error text, using a harmless reproduction if one is needed.
